findings.title: Canonical success publication is not no-replace and can falsely return success with the sealed work tree nested below an attacker-created result directory
findings.evidence: Runner line 308 uses mv "${work}" "${result}" after only the earlier line-240 precheck. A fresh temp-directory attack created destination result after precheck semantics; GNU mv returned rc=0 and produced result/stage/RUN_COMPLETE.txt rather than a canonical-root receipt. The runner then sets complete=1 and removes traps at lines 309-310, so this collision can exit successfully without a canonical sealed result root.
findings.impact: The exact runner can report success while the canonical directory is not the reviewed result layout. This violates atomic fail-closed publication and blocks authorization of a VCS candidate.
findings.required_repair: Use an independently reviewed atomic no-replace publish primitive (for example renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)) from a sibling staging directory and then verify the canonical-root RUN_COMPLETE, receipt, SHA256SUMS, and outer seal. Add a destination-created-after-precheck negative proving nonzero exit and no nested stage.

findings.title: Attempt consumption and failure trapping have an unsealed pre-trap gap
findings.evidence: Runner lines 247-253 create the final attempt directory, then set an in-memory flag, create work, install traps, and only afterwards write ATTEMPT.txt. A failure or signal between mkdir attempt and trap installation leaves an empty/mutable final attempt with no sealed attempt receipt and no sealed failure quarantine. The attempt directory is never double-sealed on the normal path.
findings.impact: One-attempt exclusion is operationally sticky but not auditable or atomically coupled to failure evidence.
findings.required_repair: Build and double-seal the attempt receipt in a sibling staging directory, atomically no-replace publish it, install cleanup coverage before any fallible post-consumption step, and add a source-only injected post-consumption failure regression that yields a sealed failure receipt.

findings.title: JSON authority gates accept duplicate object keys
findings.evidence: verify_source_contract and json_gate use plain json.loads. The source test has undefined-function and SHA negatives but no duplicate-key negative. Python therefore accepts ambiguous status/authorization/identity objects using last-key-wins semantics.
findings.impact: Future candidate/release/final-hammer authority objects are not syntactically unique under the runner's own parser, weakening exact identity closure.
findings.required_repair: Use object_pairs_hook duplicate-key rejection for every authority JSON parse and add a Python-3.6 negative for duplicate status, authorization.launch_now, and identity SHA keys.

decision.authorized_next_action: One additive source-only successor may retain all M803 RTL/SVA/TB and frozen exact-cycle gates while repairing only runner/contract identity, atomic no-replace attempt/result/failure publication, and duplicate-key rejection; it then requires a fresh independent source hammer.
